title: Check generated variant registration and callers before reproducing a local anomaly
applies_when: A candidate comes from a partial window of generated, shape- or dtype-specialized kernel code, especially a low-level binding, reusable helper or host wrapper with separate autotuning and execution paths.
lesson: Trace registry and host dtype/shape dispatch before treating a physical kernel as the API contract. Follow output dtype through allocation, autotuner eligibility and launch; a downstream validator may reject a mismatch before JIT, so it is not yet memory corruption. Inspect registration decorators themselves: a register_fake name can wrap a no-op, leaving the apparent fake function unavailable to the compiler. Check the actual dispatcher and a positive registration control before attributing a tracing failure. Require an actual helper call and substitute specialized dimensions into padding/index arithmetic: bf16 keys, aligned padding and unused helpers can refute a local premise. Equal shared-memory bases may be synchronized producer/consumer views of one buffer. Trace real pointer uses and lowered offsets, not unreferenced macros. A reduction stride may depend on fixed grid, partial allocation and final fold: changing one breaks the contract. Follow scales through final store conversion, not shuffled variable names. Static checks refute only their scoped premise, not native execution.
avoid_when: Do not exclude all generated code or assume an unregistered shape is necessarily acceptable API behavior. A shared quantization kind need not imply symmetric weight/activation storage: MXFP4/MXFP8 can use packed FP4 weights with unpacked E4M3 activations. Read the role-specific dtype/shape table and staging allocation before borrowing another role's unpacking path. Reopen with a supported logical key routed to the wrong variant, a reachable consumer of unwritten bytes, or real registration/helper calls and compiler/runtime evidence. Static reachability and arithmetic are not native numerical correctness, performance or portability tests.

evidence.note: MiniMax-H3 fp8pv launches 512 CTAs, allocates 512 partials and reads two 256-entry chunks. An unused gridDim variable does not establish skipped work; static evidence only.
Normalization decodes E4M3-rounded scales; final stores apply the same rounding. This refutes unrounded-scale storage, not every lane layout or numerical error.
W4A4 allocates the requested dtype but hardcodes BF16 for launch and tuner eligibility. Inspect all three stages.
The downstream wrapper rejects a provided output with the wrong dtype before kernel compilation. The source mismatch does not by itself establish memory corruption.

CPU metadata: three FP16 failures and three BF16 controls became six passes after dtype alignment. Real buffers/eligibility, mocked kernel. Existing author owns execution fix; feedback contributes tuner coverage, not GPU/performance qualification.

KERNELS maps architecture and logical dtype/shape/fold keys to physical generated modules. kernel_module_name rejects missing keys before loading a binding; the two inspected K8192 folded quantizers are bf16 keys, not shared fp16 implementations.

prepare_nvfp4_per_token_quantize derives the logical key from the actual input dtype. padded_sf_cols and the fixed K=8192 generated quantizer explain why a scale-column padding branch can be empty without missing required columns.

The suspect mbarrier_wait_relaxed_hint appears only as a definition in this complete translation unit, not a call or address reference. This is a scoped counterexample to inferring an active wait-ordering bug from the helper window alone.

TMA writes SFB through smem_v3..v6; after tma_full, MMA reads larger smem_v7/v8 views at the same base. They coexist; operands use pointers/lowered offsets, not the unreferenced macros. Same base need not mean independent-buffer overwrite; no native/full synchronization qualification.
The mixed mxfp4_mxfp8 kind uses E4M3 activations with full hidden width but half-width packed weights. Role-specific storage refutes assuming identical unpacking; not a native SM107 qualification.
The activation helper converts FP8 directly while the weight helper unpacks FP4 for the same kind. CPU helper checks do not qualify the full package or GPU.

The public DSA host validates strides modulo eight BF16 elements and base alignment modulo 16 bytes before binding selection. A generated byte-offset check need not duplicate the caller contract; raw bindings and internal backward layouts remain separate.
Host-validator tests distinguish supported strided layouts from rejected stride/base alignment. Existing controls support reading the caller, not full native GPU correctness.

Both Torch-version branches return identity decorators for register_custom_op and register_fake_op. Names do not establish dispatcher registration. This refutes attributing a compiler metadata failure to a dormant fake, not every compile compatibility problem.
Real and fake expert SwiGLU wrappers both derive k=input.shape[-1]//2 before FP4 byte packing. A truncated view created the false premise that only the fake divides twice.
